landmarks.name: Grand Palace
landmarks.writeup: A historic royal residence in Bangkok, known for its intricate architecture and the Emerald Buddha.

landmarks.name: Ayutthaya Historical Park
landmarks.writeup: Ruins of the ancient capital city, showcasing temples and palaces from the 14th to 18th centuries.

landmarks.name: Phi Phi Islands
landmarks.writeup: Famous tropical islands known for clear waters, coral reefs, and vibrant marine life.

landmarks.name: Wat Arun
landmarks.writeup: The Temple of Dawn, a riverside Buddhist temple noted for its towering spires decorated with colorful porcelain.

landmarks.name: Doi Inthanon National Park
landmarks.writeup: Home to Thailand's highest peak, featuring waterfalls, hiking trails, and diverse flora and fauna.

cultural_events.name: Songkran Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Thai New Year celebrated with water fights, religious rituals, and family gatherings in April.

cultural_events.name: Loy Krathong
cultural_events.writeup: Festival of lights where people float decorated baskets on water to pay respects to the water spirits.

cultural_events.name: Yi Peng Lantern Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated mainly in northern Thailand, releasing lanterns into the sky for good luck.

food_writeup: Thai cuisine is known for its balance of sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors, featuring dishes like Pad Thai, Tom Yum soup, and green curry, often using fresh herbs and spices.
brief_history: Thailand, formerly Siam, has a history dating back to the 13th century with the Sukhothai Kingdom. It is unique in Southeast Asia for never having been colonized by a European power. The country transitioned from absolute monarchy to constitutional monarchy in 1932.

important_people.name: Prem Tinsulanonda
important_people.description: influential former Prime Minister and Regent

current_conflicts: Thailand faces ongoing political tensions and occasional protests related to governance and monarchy reforms, but no active armed conflicts.
